question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **See eye to eye**

options.text: To understand a complex visual concept
To agree fully with someone else

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. To agree fully with someone else .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"See eye to eye"** means to be in complete agreement with someone.
 
• It is often used when two or more people share the same opinion or perspective on a matter.
 
• It does not mean to stare at someone, to understand a visual concept, or to disagree with someone, as mentioned in the other options.

Correct sentence: *The two leaders finally saw **eye to eye** on the trade agreement.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin:** The phrase has biblical origins and is said to come from the Book of Isaiah in the Bible, referring to complete agreement or unity.
 
• **Usage Example:** Despite their differences, the team members saw eye to eye on the final strategy for the project.
